question.name: CSEC Chem May 2023 Q1a(i)(ii) — Define Rate of Reaction and Catalyst
question.text:
(i) Define the term 'rate of reaction': (1 mark)

Rate of reaction = change in [[1]] ÷ [[2]]

(ii) Define the term 'catalyst': (2 marks)

A catalyst [[3]] the rate of reaction without being [[4]] itself; it [[5]] the activation energy needed.
question.general_feedback:
Rate of reaction:

Rate of reaction = change in concentration (or amount) ÷ time

Units: mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹ (or mol s⁻¹ if using amounts)

Catalyst:

A catalyst increases (speeds up) the rate of reaction without being used up (consumed/chemically changed) itself; it lowers (reduces) the activation energy needed for the reaction.

How catalysts work: They provide an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy — more reactant particles have enough energy to react, so the reaction proceeds faster.

Note: Catalysts are not consumed — they are regenerated and can catalyse the same reaction repeatedly. The catalyst is unchanged at the end of the reaction.

groups.label: Rate of reaction = change in ___ per unit time
groups.diagnostic_hint: Rate of reaction = change in concentration (or amount) per unit time. You can also express it as change in mass, volume of gas, or absorbance per unit time.

groups.label: Rate of reaction = change in concentration per unit ___
groups.diagnostic_hint: The "per unit" part is per unit TIME (e.g., per second, per minute). Rate has units of mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹ or g s⁻¹, etc.

groups.label: Catalyst — ___ the rate of reaction
groups.diagnostic_hint: A catalyst INCREASES (speeds up) the rate of reaction by providing an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.

groups.label: Catalyst — is NOT ___ during the reaction
groups.diagnostic_hint: A catalyst is NOT used up (consumed) in the reaction — it remains chemically unchanged at the end. This is what makes it a catalyst (not a reactant).

groups.label: Catalyst — ___ the activation energy
groups.diagnostic_hint: A catalyst LOWERS (reduces) the activation energy, allowing more molecules to have sufficient energy to react, thus increasing the rate.

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 19 tokens for 5 slots. Slot 1 (concentration/amount): both accepted as equivalent representations of how much reactant is present. 'Temperature' is wrong — temperature is a factor affecting rate, not the numerator of the rate expression. Slot 2 (time): the rate denominator; 'volume' is wrong — volume may appear in concentration (mol/dm³) but is not itself the denominator. Slot 3 (increases/speeds up): catalyst increases rate; 'decreases' describes an inhibitor. Slot 4 (used up/chemically changed): the 1m slot — students often think catalysts are consumed (they aren't). Slot 5 (lowers/reduces): catalyst lowers activation energy; 'raises' is the opposite and is wrong.
